title: Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He spoke in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4 and Taanit, chapter 2, end of halakhah 1.
And in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4, Shekalim, beginning of chapter 3, and Avodah Zarah 2:8.
In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:4: Rabbi Tanchuma bar Chiyya in the name of Rabbi Simlai.
In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:7: Rabbi Yasa went up to Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya and wanted to move it from before him (the lamp, on Shabbat). Rabbi Tanchum said to him: “In our presence?”

In Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:7: Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa went up to Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya, who was in mourning, and he came out to meet him in garments that were not rent. He said to him: “From where do you have this?” Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya said to him: “So my master Rabbi Simon used to do,” and he asked Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa to pray for him.
Bereshit Rabbah 100:7 reads Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya of Kefar Agin.

In Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:2: “Rabbi Kahana said: I was a chaver, and Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya brought me in for the sanctification of the new month,” etc. Of those who speak in his name we find Rabbi Achar in the name of Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya, as in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:3 and Taanit, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1, and there chapter 2, end of halakhah 1; and Hyman proposes this reading in Pesikta deRav Kahana 166.

Rabbi Lazar son of Rabbi Yose (the Amora) in his name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Maaserot 1:3 and Moed Katan 1:1; and at the end of Avodah Zarah, chapter 1, “Rabbi Acha, Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya in the name of Rabbi Lazar son of Rabbi Yose” — Hyman considers undoubtedly correct the reading “Rabbi Acha and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yose in the name of Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiyya.”
Rabbi Chananyah son of Rabbi Ada in his name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:4.
Rabbi Yudan in his name, as in Bereshit Rabbah 6:3.
Rabbi Yonah in his name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:1 and Taanit, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1.
In Yalkut, Isaiah, remez 317: Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Tanchum bar Chiyya.

notes.text: The chapter:halakhah references here are Jerusalem Talmud. Saved Guggenheimer Shabbat3:7 places Yasa’s visit in the lamp-removal dispute; Yasa wants to remove the lamp and Tanchum objects in our presence, avoiding the draft’s attachment to Tanchum. ר׳ אחאר remains Achar and כמעשות is read Maaserot, as disclosed previously. Tanchum asks Chinena to pray for him. Hyman’s confident chain reversal remains a proposal.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:7 places Yasa as the one wanting to remove the lamp, with Tanchum objecting in our presence. The current mourning/prayer actor direction, Achar and Maaserot disclosures are retained. Hyman’s undoubtedly correct chain reversal remains his proposed repartition, not an independent name or authority merger.
